extracted.intended_audience: academic librarians and research-impact practitioners (university faculty who request impact reports)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, implementing, and assessing a library-run Policy & News Media Impact Service that produces reports demonstrating faculty research impact in policy documents and news media. Covers intake, resources, workflow, inclusion/exclusion rules, reporting template, evaluation, and operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the Policy & News Media Impact Service is to describe a broader scope of the research impact of individual scholars in public policy and media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide faculty with data points beyond citation counts for uses such as promotion/tenure dossiers and grant applications; acknowledge this captures only one aspect of impact and should be contextualized within discipline and career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report template structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Template is organized at a broad level—policies, guidelines, and government documents, and media coverage—and then subdivided into different categories, each of which includes a list of relevant citations. Prefaced with an executive summary that provides an overview of the results and highlights notable references in policy or news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the executive summary to highlight notable references; subdivide results for clarity (policy vs media); include lists of relevant citations under each category. (See supplemental Appendix A for template example.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Intake information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Online intake form in which faculty indicate the scope and intended use of the report and provide links to or lists of their relevant grants or publications. Faculty could choose to provide their entire curriculum vita or focus on a subset of publications (e.g., last five years or particular research interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place no limits on number of publications included (but explicitly exclude certain research outputs like conference presentations); use intake to triage eligibility and set project template. Capture intended use (e.g., promotion, grant) to tailor report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for requestors
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pilot, eligibility was limited to faculty in selected departments; to make a request, at least one individual was required to be a faculty member in one of these departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define eligibility (departmental or center-based) clearly during pilot/launch and expand later as capacity permits. State eligibility on service web page and intake form to streamline triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround time and staff-effort cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports were completed within two weeks of a request, except where other arrangements were made, and the team committed to devoting no more than twenty hours to the completion of any single report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set and communicate realistic turnaround expectations and a maximum staff-hour cap per report to control workload and plan staffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data security and report delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a secure, cloud-based storage system (Box) with encryption and two-factor authentication; access limited to collaborators and previous versions maintained. Completed report transmitted to requestor as a PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose institutional storage with version control and secure access; restrict access to collaborators; deliver final reports in portable, non-editable format (PDF) while keeping source files for internal versioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource selection and prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify a set of subscription-based and publicly available resources covering policy and news media; prioritize core resources due to coverage and utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a curated list of tools (both subscription and public); mark core/prioritized resources; balance subscription costs against coverage and staff time. See Table 1 for resources used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of social media from primary scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media platforms such as Facebook and Twitter were not included due to issues surrounding scalability and because social media activities often act as 'pointers to research' rather than providing substantive commentary aligned with the service purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude social media when service aims to document substantive policy/media engagement; if social media is included, be explicit about different counting methods and resource implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization of team members and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members specialized in particular tools and areas rather than building capacity across all resources; newer team members split responsibilities rather than complete reports independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign staff to specific tools/areas (e.g., government publications, newspapers) to streamline workflows, minimize duplicate effort, and reduce training burden; use biweekly meetings to discuss strategies and challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules for duplicated/syndicated content
rubrics_metrics.description: When one item authored by one individual is reproduced in a variety of other publications (syndication), the team chose to count the original item rather than its reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and document counting decisions (e.g., count original item vs reproductions), because different count types (number of posts NP vs number of unique users NUU) convey different messages and affect altmetrics interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Altmetrics count-type transparency (NP vs NUU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two primary ways to count altmetrics activities: number of unique users (NUU) and number of posts (NP); NP can be larger than NUU and these indicators have only moderate-to-low correlation, indicating they convey different messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly which count type is used for each metric; inform requestors about implications of chosen counting method for interpretation of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-curation / inclusion policy for criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: The service chose not to curate reports, meaning all aspects of broader engagement were included, including when a researcher’s work is criticized; position: 'impact and agreement are not synonymous.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include negative engagement as evidence of substantive engagement; document philosophical stance on curation and how negative mentions are presented to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research outputs included
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports included publications (faculty could provide CV or subset); other research outputs, such as conference presentations, were not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define included output types on intake form; be explicit about exclusions (conference presentations, teaching/clinical work) so requestors know what the report will and will not represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search constraints and techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches for some tools (e.g., Google) were restricted using domain and format limits; search tips for resources were recorded and shared within the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and share search strategies and constraints for each resource; record tips in a shared document to ensure consistency and efficiency across staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverable usability and format expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty found it very easy to find service web page/form, complete the form, work with the team, and understand the final report; deliverable format: Word document maintained internally, transmitted as PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the report format is clear and accessible to faculty; use an executive summary and clear sections to increase usability for promotion and grant uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and feedback metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot assessed via a survey asking about recommendation likelihood, usefulness for intended purposes, ease of engaging with service aspects, and free-text suggestions; results used to refine service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement user surveys after report delivery to measure satisfaction (recommendation, usefulness, ease) and gather qualitative feedback for improvements (e.g., desire for clearer methodology or indication of most influential publications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and contextualization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports capture one aspect of research impact and are not representative of the full scope of a researcher’s influence; policy impact is often a medium- to long-term measure and linking particular publication to particular policy decision is problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contextual statements in reports noting limitations (e.g., doesn't capture teaching/service/clinical contributions; linkage between publications and policy decisions is nuanced); encourage use of reports as part of broader evidence of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff training and resource-cost considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports represent a significant investment of staff resources for both production and development of necessary skills; medical librarian search skills may not transfer to non-health resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for staff training needs and time costs; weigh subscription costs against staff time; use staff specialization to reduce training time per individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation/tool limitations and customization value
rubrics_metrics.description: No single altmetrics tool provides the comprehensive, customized end product most valuable to users; due to ephemeral nature of materials no tool can claim to be comprehensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider combining tools and manual searching to produce a customized report; balance automation with human curation to meet users' needs; evaluate subscription vs manual approach in terms of cost and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and uptake strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing the service was a primary challenge; most faculty learned of the service via colleagues rather than library marketing efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage peer recommendation and targeted outreach to likely users (e.g., around promotion/tenure cycles); anticipate increased requests for updates to reports when faculty prepare dossiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request granularity and potential scaling responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports were completed for individuals and small groups; no centers or departments requested service yet; if broader requests occur, timelines and workflows would be adjusted to account for workload increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan scalability strategies (e.g., different timelines, team composition, caps on hours, alternative service tiers) in advance to respond to larger-scope requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire for explicit influence indicators (which publications most influential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty expressed interest in providing greater information on which publications had been most influential and providing more explicit methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider adding indicators or an explicit methodology section in reports showing relative influence of individual publications (e.g., which items were most cited in policy or media), and document methods so users can interpret results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy on impact vs agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophical stance: impact and agreement are not synonymous; negative citation or criticism can still be an indicator of impact because 'it is somewhat of an achievement to have one’s work noticed by others, even if negatively.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and make explicit a philosophy that recognizes negative attention as engagement; present negative mentions neutrally as evidence of substantive engagement rather than as failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cases to tailor report content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports were predominantly requested for supplementing promotion and tenure dossiers or for grant applications; requestors were chiefly interested in policy coverage, followed by news and media coverage, then blogs and other web content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask requestors their intended use (promotion, grant, other) and prioritize findings accordingly (e.g., emphasize policy citations for promotion dossiers in policy-oriented disciplines).
